lead: As gain K rises from 0 to ∞, closed-loop poles move along fixed paths: the root locus. Eight rules draw them from open-loop poles and zeros alone. The locus helps choose a gain for desired overshoot and settling time, and place compensator poles and zeros. It is a first pass when tuning a motor drive or a temperature loop.
prereq: You need 3.1 for 1 + G H = 0, 3.2 for the Routh jω crossing, and Unit 1 for reducing a block diagram to G(s)H(s).

blocks.text: Unity feedback with forward path K G(s) and sensor path H(s). Closed-loop poles solve:

blocks.where: K is gain (positive real); G(s)H(s) is the open-loop transfer function; s = σ + jω is complex frequency, σ real part (1/s), ω imaginary part (rad/s).

blocks.text: A complex number equals a real negative number only when magnitude and angle match:

blocks.where: q = 0, ±1, ±2, …; |·| is magnitude and ∠ is phase in degrees. The angle condition fixes shape; the magnitude condition gives K at a point.

blocks.text: The angle condition has no K. Points whose open-loop phase is an odd multiple of 180° are fixed by pole and zero positions. K only decides where along that set the poles sit. Phase at s is sum of angles from zeros minus sum from poles. A real pole or zero to the right of s adds 180°; a complex pair adds 360°, which is zero. So only the count to the right matters on the real axis.

items: Rule 1 — branches: there are n branches, where n is number of open-loop poles and m is number of open-loop zeros.
Rule 2 — symmetry: real coefficients give conjugate poles, so the locus mirrors about the real axis.
Rule 3 — endpoints: at K = 0 a branch starts at an open-loop pole. As K → ∞ it ends at an open-loop zero; remaining n − m go to infinity.
Rule 4 — real axis: a point is on the locus when real poles and zeros strictly to its right total an odd count. Test intervals, not individual poles.
Rule 5 — asymptotes: the n − m branches to infinity have angles (2q + 1)180°/(n − m) and meet at centroid σ = (Σ poles − Σ zeros)/(n − m), using real parts only.
Rule 6 — breakaway: where branches meet and split, dK/ds = 0. From K = −1/(G H), differentiate, solve, and keep roots on a rule-4 segment.
Rule 7 — jω crossing: put the characteristic polynomial in a Routh array. The gain where the s¹ row vanishes makes the loop marginal; the auxiliary equation from the s² row gives ω.

Rule 8 — departure angle: at a complex pole p, θ_d = 180° + (sum of angles from other poles to p) − (sum of angles from zeros to p). For arrival at a complex zero, reverse the signs: θ_a = 180° + Σ(angles from zeros) − Σ(angles from poles).

blocks.text: Rules 1 to 5 fix the skeleton. Rules 6 to 8 give the numbers an examiner asks for.
Use G(s)H(s) = K/(s(s + 2)(s + 4)) with unity feedback. The poles are 0, −2, −4; there are no zeros, so n = 3 and m = 0.

items: Three branches start at 0, −2, −4 and all run to infinity.
Real-axis parts are (−2, 0) and (−∞, −4). The stretch (−4, −2) has two poles to its right, so it is not on the locus.
The centroid is (0 − 2 − 4)/3 = −2. Asymptote angles are 60°, 180° and 300°, from −2.
The branches from 0 and −2 meet at breakaway s = −0.85, K = 3.1. They leave as a complex pair, bend toward 60° and 300°, and cross to the right half plane at K = 48, ω = 2.83 rad/s.

blocks.text: Add a pole at −6: n − m = 4, so asymptote angles are 45°, 135°, 225°, 315° and centroid is −3. Breakaway moves to about s = −0.77 (K ≈ 16), and the jω crossing moves to K = 160 at ω = 2 rad/s. A pole does not always lower critical gain; work the Routh array. Add a zero at −1: n − m = 2, asymptotes are 90° and 270°, centroid is (0 − 2 − 4 + 1)/2 = −2.5. The zero attracts a branch and bends the complex pair left. The loop is stable for every K > 0. That leftward pull is why a compensator zero is placed before a slow pole (see Unit 5, Controllers and Compensators).

figure.caption: Construction order for K/(s(s+2)(s+4)). The asymptote centroid is −2 even though no pole is there. Branches reach the right half plane at K = 48.

spec.title: Sketching K/(s(s+2)(s+4))
spec.aria: Top-to-bottom construction of the root locus for K divided by s times s plus 2 times s plus 4, from open-loop poles to finished sketch, with asymptotes and j-omega crossing marked.

examples.question: A unity feedback loop has G(s)H(s) = K/(s(s + 2)(s + 4)). Sketch the root locus and find the gain K at marginal stability, with the oscillation frequency there.
steps: Poles 0, −2, −4; no zeros. n = 3, m = 0; three branches go to infinity.
Real-axis parts: (−2, 0) and (−∞, −4). (−4, −2) is not on the locus.
Reject −3.155: it lies in (−4, −2), not on the locus. Breakaway is s = −0.845.
Characteristic equation: s³ + 6s² + 8s + K = 0. Routh rows: s³: 1, 8; s²: 6, K; s¹: (48 − K)/6; s⁰: K.
Auxiliary equation: 6s² + K = 0. With K = 48, s² = −8, so ω = 2.83 rad/s.
examples.answer: The locus has branches at poles 0, −2, −4; real-axis parts (−2, 0) and (−∞, −4); asymptotes 60°, 180°, −60° from centroid −2; breakaway s = −0.845 with K ≈ 3.1. The loop is marginal at K = 48, oscillating at ω = 2.83 rad/s.
examples.check:
import math
n,m=3,0
sigma=(0-2-4)/n
angles=[(2*q+1)*180/(n-m) for q in (0,1,-1)]
a,b,c=3,12,8
disc=b*b-4*a*c
r1=(-b+math.sqrt(disc))/(2*a)
r2=(-b-math.sqrt(disc))/(2*a)
brk=max(r1,r2)
K_brk=-(brk**3+6*brk**2+8*brk)
K_cross=48.0
omega=math.sqrt(K_cross/6)
print("roots of dK/ds =",round(r1,3),round(r2,3))
print("breakaway s =",round(brk,3))
print("K at breakaway =",round(K_brk,2))
print("centroid =",sigma)
print("asymptote angles =",[round(x,1) for x in angles])
print("K at crossing =",K_cross)
print("omega at crossing =",round(omega,2))

traps: Accepting every root of dK/ds = 0. Here −3.155 lies in (−4, −2), not on the locus, so reject it. Test roots against rule 4.
Writing n asymptotes instead of n − m. With n = 3 and m = 1, use two at 90° and 270°.
Forgetting zeros in rule 4. Count both real poles and real zeros to the right.

Calling every touch a breakaway. A root of dK/ds = 0 on the locus is a breakaway if branches leave the real axis; it is a break-in if they arrive. Decide by branch direction, or by local minimum or maximum of K along that segment.
Reading the crossing frequency from the s¹ row. The s¹ row gives K; the auxiliary equation from the s² row gives ω.

quiz.q: State the angle condition and magnitude condition for the root locus.
quiz.a: ∠G(s)H(s) = (2q + 1)180°, q = 0, ±1, ±2, …, and |G(s)H(s)| = 1/K. Angle fixes shape; magnitude gives K at a point.

quiz.q: Why is the root locus symmetric about the real axis?
quiz.a: Real coefficients give complex roots in conjugate pairs. If σ + jω is a pole at some K, σ − jω is also a pole at the same K.

quiz.q: A system has four open-loop poles and one open-loop zero. How many branches go to infinity, and at what angles?
For G(s)H(s) = K/(s(s + 2)(s + 4)) with unity feedback, find the breakaway point and gain there.
Use Routh's array on G(s)H(s) = K/(s(s + 2)(s + 4)) with unity feedback to find marginal-stability gain and oscillation frequency.
quiz.a: s³ + 6s² + 8s + K = 0. Routh: s³: 1, 8; s²: 6, K; s¹: (48 − K)/6; s⁰: K. s¹ row vanishes at K = 48. Auxiliary 6s² + 48 = 0 gives ω = 2.83 rad/s.

quiz.q: A zero at s = −1 is added to G(s)H(s) = K/(s(s + 2)(s + 4)). Explain asymptotes, centroid and stability limit.
quiz.a: n = 3, m = 1, so n − m = 2 branches at 90° and 270°. Centroid = (0 − 2 − 4 + 1)/2 = −2.5. Branch from 0 runs to zero −1; branches from −2 and −4 meet between −4 and −2 and leave as a complex pair. For s³ + 6s² + (8 + K)s + K = 0, the s¹ row is (48 + 5K)/6, positive for all K > 0. Stable for all K > 0; no finite crossing.

quiz.q: Both s = −0.845 and s = −3.155 solve dK/ds = 0 in the third-order example. Which is the breakaway point, and why reject the other?
quiz.a: Rule 4 puts the locus on (−2, 0) and (−∞, −4). s = −0.845 lies in (−2, 0), so it is breakaway. s = −3.155 lies in (−4, −2), which has no branch, so discard it.

beyond: Not for the exam. MATLAB rlocus and Python control.root_locus sweep K and find characteristic roots; the rules are shortcuts. The locus is the picture behind pole placement (Unit 6, State Space Analysis).
